learning: Iterations 8 and 10 each tested one lever (mass 0.5, wheel_track 0.11) and both lowered the score. The result is sensitive to single parameters, so this design is kept as delivered.
notes: Final candidate: the iteration 7 and 9 design, unchanged from entity0. The controller is the proven one (kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, 25 times x weights, last_direction). Reproduced exactly at iteration 9 with score 75.9247.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design raced once on the unseen track is scored and nothing can be revised afterwards. The evidence favours the proven best design. Iterations 7 and 9 reproduced exactly (score 75.9247, oval progress 0.2725, s-bend progress 0.1573 with oscillation 0.135, slalom progress 0.1094 with 1.0 line loss per run), so the simulator is deterministic for this design. Every single-lever change tested from it lowered the score: mass 0.5 (iteration 8, 55.18), and wheel_track 0.11 (iteration 10, 54.95, with oval progress back to 0.1225). I therefore adopt the Builder's entity0 geometry without change: mass 0.6, forward lead y = 0.08 (the contract maximum), 16 mm sensors at x = -0.08 to 0.08 in 0.04 m steps, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.16 by 0.14 m. The controller is the same as iterations 3 to 9: kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, sensor weights 25 times x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), and last_direction line-loss recovery. The controller is unchanged, so the only thing that can differ from iteration 9 is the unseen track. The risk is that the unseen track is of a different shape and the design's sensitivity to mass and track width does not transfer. I accept that risk, because any alternative is untested here and would be a guess.
